claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component state migrations are a new feature.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A component state migrations discussion exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.

The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, creating a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway, with a security group outside the component.
Replacing an AWS VPC requires replacing a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data, and the example does not create a database.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

The resource trees Pulumi tracks in v1 (legacy awsx:x:ec2 component types), v2 (awsx:ec2:Vpc), and v3 (plain aws resources) are as shown, with subnet name changing from vpc-isolated-0 to vpc-isolated-1.
Pulumi state records resources and components, each with a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts managed resources under different parents.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Pulumi resources accept a `stateMigrations` option taking a migration callback, and an alias for the legacy component type.

The migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (complete replacement records) and `successors` (map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
The migration callback is idempotent: if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources it does nothing, and an unexpected component type raises an error.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent while preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses the `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid after migration.
The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and maps both the old component and its VPC child to the new VPC record, which keeps its AWS ID.

Pulumi runs migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration, and after both have run both callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
For the example upgrades, the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group should show no creates, deletes, or replacements in preview.
When a component ships a registered migration, users do not need to write the migration or edit stack state; Pulumi runs it as part of normal preview and update.
For an internal component change that keeps the same inputs and outputs, users can keep their existing component calls.
The component state migrations guide in the Pulumi docs covers the callback contract, and the VPC example contains all three programs and the migration code.
State migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during Pulumi previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite resource state without performing provider operations.

A Pulumi component state migration (stateMigrations resource option callback) is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/ has a callback-api section explaining the callback API.

State entries passed to component state migration callbacks use the checkpoint resource format, documented at the Pulumi developer docs deployment-schema page (pulumi-resource-state), including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans and targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
